sources.title: Veltrano Maps pricing: credits and overage
sources.text:
Veltrano Maps bills API usage in credits. A forward or reverse geocoding request uses 1 credit, a route optimisation request uses 5 credits, and a static map image uses 2 credits. Each plan includes a monthly credit allowance: Sandbox includes 10,000 credits, Builder includes 400,000 credits and Scale includes 6,000,000 credits. Unused credits expire at the end of the billing month and do not roll over.

Usage beyond the allowance is charged as overage at the end of the month. Builder overage costs $0.60 per 1,000 credits and Scale overage costs $0.35 per 1,000 credits. Sandbox projects cannot incur overage; once the allowance is used up, further requests return HTTP 402 until the next billing month begins.

You can set a monthly spending cap from the billing page. When the cap is reached, Veltrano Maps sends an email to every project owner and stops serving billable requests until the cap is raised or the month ends. Changes to the cap take effect within five minutes.

sources.title: Rate limits for the Veltrano Maps REST API
sources.text:
Every request to the Veltrano Maps REST API counts toward a per-project limit measured in requests per second (RPS). The limit depends on the plan the project is billed under:

- Sandbox: 5 RPS for geocoding and 2 RPS for route optimisation.
- Builder: 50 RPS for geocoding and 10 RPS for route optimisation.
- Scale: 400 RPS for geocoding and 60 RPS for route optimisation.

Scale projects may burst to 800 RPS on geocoding for up to 30 seconds, provided the project has a verified billing contact on file. Bursting is not available on Sandbox or Builder projects.

When a project goes over its limit, the API responds with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header giving the number of seconds to wait before retrying. Requests rejected with HTTP 429 are not billed. Limits are applied per project, not per API key, so creating additional keys within the same project does not raise the ceiling.

If you need a higher sustained limit than your plan provides, contact the solutions team from the project dashboard. Requests for custom limits are reviewed within five business days.

sources.title: Map tiles: connection limits and caching
sources.text:
Map tiles are served from a separate content delivery network and are not counted toward the REST API limits described elsewhere in this documentation. Instead, tile traffic is limited by the number of concurrent connections a project can hold open: 4 on Sandbox, 32 on Builder and 256 on Scale.

Vector tiles are cached at the edge for 24 hours and raster tiles for 7 days. If you restyle a map, add a new style version to the tile URL so that clients fetch fresh tiles instead of waiting for the cache to expire.

Tile requests must include the project's public token, which begins with pk_. Public tokens are safe to embed in browser and mobile code because they can only read tiles and styles; they cannot call geocoding or routing endpoints. You can restrict a public token to a list of allowed referrer domains or mobile bundle identifiers from the token settings page. Requests from a domain that is not on the list receive HTTP 403.

items.question: Do Corvane Ledger refresh tokens expire?
items.answer: In the EU data region, refresh tokens expire after 30 days of inactivity.

sources.title: Using the Corvane Ledger sandbox
sources.text:
Every developer account includes a sandbox workspace that mirrors the production API but holds only test data. Sandbox requests go to a separate host, shown in the developer console, and use their own client ID and client secret, which you create under Sandbox apps. Credentials from one environment are rejected by the other.

The sandbox is seeded with a sample company that has 18 months of journal history, a chart of accounts with 64 accounts, and 40 customer and supplier contacts. You can reset the sandbox to this starting state at any time; a reset takes about two minutes and deletes everything you created.

Sandbox data is also wiped automatically on the first Sunday of each quarter. Reports generated in the sandbox carry a SANDBOX watermark, and email notifications from the sandbox go only to the developer account's own address, never to the contacts stored in the test company.

sources.title: Corvane Ledger API: scopes reference
sources.text:
Scopes control what an access token is allowed to do. Request only the scopes your integration needs; users see the full list on the consent screen and are more likely to approve a short one.

- ledger:read - read journals, accounts and balances.
- ledger:write - create and reverse journal entries. Implies ledger:read.
- reports:read - download trial balance, profit and loss, and aged receivables reports.
- contacts:manage - create, update and archive customer and supplier records.
- webhooks:manage - register and remove webhook endpoints for the workspace.

A token that lacks the scope required by an endpoint receives HTTP 403 with the error code insufficient_scope. Scopes cannot be added to an existing token. To gain a new scope, send the user through the consent flow again; the new access token and refresh token replace the old pair.

Workspace administrators can see every integration that holds a token for their workspace, along with its scopes, under Settings > Connected apps, and can disconnect an integration at any time.

sources.title: Authenticating with the Corvane Ledger API
sources.text:
The Corvane Ledger API uses OAuth 2.0. Your integration exchanges an authorisation code, or for server-to-server use its client ID and client secret, at the /oauth/token endpoint and receives an access token together with a refresh token.

Access tokens are valid for 60 minutes from the time they are issued. Send them in the Authorization header as a bearer token. A request made with an expired access token returns HTTP 401 with the error code token_expired; your client should then obtain a new access token using its refresh token rather than sending the user back through consent.

In the EU data region, refresh tokens expire after 30 days of inactivity. This rule supports the data-minimisation commitments in our EU processing terms. Every successful use of a refresh token resets its inactivity timer.

Client secrets can be rotated from the developer console. After a rotation, the previous secret continues to work for 24 hours so you can update your deployments without downtime. Rotating a secret does not invalidate access tokens or refresh tokens that were already issued.

sources.title: Hollowmere Commerce API: paginating list endpoints
sources.text:
List endpoints return results one page at a time. Each response body contains a data array and a page_info object with two fields, has_more and next_page_token. To fetch the following page, repeat the same request with the page_token query parameter set to the value of next_page_token, and stop when has_more is false.

Page size is controlled with the page_size query parameter, which defaults to 25. Most list endpoints accept a page_size of up to 100. From 1 September 2026 to 31 January 2027, the /v2/orders endpoint accepts a page_size of up to 500 to help merchants move their order exports off the retired CSV feed. A request that asks for more than the permitted maximum is rejected with HTTP 400 and the error code page_size_too_large; it is never silently truncated.

Page tokens are opaque and are bound to the filters and sort order of the request that produced them. If you change a filter between pages, the API returns HTTP 409 with the error code page_token_mismatch. A page token remains usable for 6 hours after it is issued.

Results are ordered by updated_at, newest first. A record that changes while you are paginating can appear again on a later page, so deduplicate on the id field.

sources.title: Filtering orders
sources.text:
The /v2/orders endpoint accepts filters as query parameters. Combine as many as you need; they are joined with AND.

- status: one of pending, paid, fulfilled, refunded or cancelled. Pass several values separated by commas to match any of them.
- created_after and created_before: ISO 8601 timestamps. Both bounds are exclusive.
- channel: web, pos or marketplace.
- customer_id: return only orders placed by one customer.

Free-text search over order notes and customer names is handled by the separate /v2/orders/search endpoint, which takes a q parameter of at least three characters. Search results are ranked by relevance rather than by date and are capped at 1,000 matches per query; narrow the query with filters if you need to reach older orders.

Archived orders are excluded from both endpoints unless you pass include_archived=true. Orders are archived automatically 24 months after they are fulfilled or cancelled, and archived orders cannot be edited.

sources.title: Retirement of the CSV order feed
sources.text:

Files that had already been generated remain available in the Reports area of the merchant dashboard for 90 days after the retirement date.

The recommended replacement is to read orders directly from the /v2/orders endpoint and write them to your own storage. Merchants who used the feed for accounting can instead connect one of the certified accounting integrations from the app directory, which sync paid and refunded orders every 15 minutes.

If you relied on the feed's column layout, the field mapping guide lists the API field that corresponds to each former CSV column. Two columns have no direct equivalent: gift_message, which is now part of the notes array, and warehouse_code, which moved to each fulfillment record. Contact merchant support if you need help planning the move before your next accounting close.

sources.title: Ondrel Billing webhook event types
sources.text:
Subscribe each webhook endpoint only to the events your integration handles. You can change an endpoint's subscriptions at any time; the change applies to events created after you save it.

Invoices
- invoice.created - a draft invoice was generated for a subscription or a one-off charge.
- invoice.finalized - the invoice was locked and sent to the customer.
- invoice.paid - payment succeeded in full.
- invoice.payment_failed - a payment attempt was declined or returned an error.

Subscriptions
- subscription.created, subscription.updated and subscription.cancelled.
- subscription.trial_ending - sent 3 days before a trial converts to a paid plan.

Customers
- customer.created and customer.updated.
- customer.tax_id_verified - a tax identifier passed validation.

Each event payload contains an id, a type, a created_at timestamp and a data object holding the full resource as it was when the event occurred. Events are kept in the event log for 30 days, where you can inspect payloads and see the response your endpoint returned to every attempt.

sources.title: Ondrel Billing webhooks: delivery and retries
sources.text:
Ondrel Billing sends each webhook event to your endpoint as an HTTPS POST request with a JSON body. Respond with any 2xx status within 10 seconds to acknowledge the event; slower responses are recorded as timeouts and count as failed deliveries.

Extended retries. From 1 December 2026, Ondrel Billing retries a failed webhook delivery for up to 72 hours if the endpoint has extended retries enabled. Retries use exponential backoff, starting at 1 minute and capped at 6 hours between attempts. Turn on extended retries for each endpoint under Settings > Developers > Webhooks.

Duplicates and ordering. Every attempt for the same event carries the same value in the Ondrel-Event-Id header, so your handler can discard events it has already processed. Events are not guaranteed to arrive in the order they were created; compare the created_at field in the payload if ordering matters.

Disabled endpoints. If every delivery to an endpoint has failed for 5 consecutive days, the endpoint is disabled automatically and the account owner is notified by email. Fix the underlying problem, then re-enable the endpoint from the same settings page. Events that occurred while the endpoint was disabled are not redelivered automatically, but you can replay them from the event log.

sources.title: Receiving test webhooks with the Ondrel command-line tool
sources.text:
The Ondrel command-line tool lets you receive test-mode webhook events on your own machine without exposing a public URL. After signing in with ondrel login, run ondrel listen --forward-to localhost:4000/hooks and the tool relays every test-mode event from your account to that local address.

The terminal shows each event type as it arrives, along with the status code your local server returned. To generate an event on demand, run ondrel trigger followed by an event type, for example ondrel trigger invoice.paid. Triggered events use fixture data and do not create real customers or charges.

Events relayed this way carry livemode set to false, so you can guard against processing them in production code. The listen command relays only events created while it is running; it does not fetch older events from the event log. A listen session ends after 8 hours, after which you need to run the command again. Live-mode events are never relayed by the command-line tool.

sources.title: Ondrel Billing webhook event types
sources.text:
Subscribe each webhook endpoint only to the events your integration handles. You can change an endpoint's subscriptions at any time; the change applies to events created after you save it.

Invoices
- invoice.created - a draft invoice was generated for a subscription or a one-off charge.
- invoice.finalized - the invoice was locked and sent to the customer.
- invoice.paid - payment succeeded in full.
- invoice.payment_failed - a payment attempt was declined or returned an error.

Subscriptions
- subscription.created, subscription.updated and subscription.cancelled.
- subscription.trial_ending - sent 3 days before a trial converts to a paid plan.

Customers
- customer.created and customer.updated.
- customer.tax_id_verified - a tax identifier passed validation.

Each event payload contains an id, a type, a created_at timestamp and a data object holding the full resource as it was when the event occurred. Events are kept in the event log for 30 days, where you can inspect payloads and see the response your endpoint returned to every attempt.

sources.title: Ondrel Billing webhooks: delivery and retries
sources.text:
Ondrel Billing sends each webhook event to your endpoint as an HTTPS POST request with a JSON body. Respond with any 2xx status within 10 seconds to acknowledge the event; slower responses are recorded as timeouts and count as failed deliveries.

Extended retries. From 1 December 2026, Ondrel Billing retries a failed webhook delivery for up to 72 hours if the endpoint has extended retries enabled. Retries use exponential backoff, starting at 1 minute and capped at 6 hours between attempts. Turn on extended retries for each endpoint under Settings > Developers > Webhooks.

Duplicates and ordering. Every attempt for the same event carries the same value in the Ondrel-Event-Id header, so your handler can discard events it has already processed. Events are not guaranteed to arrive in the order they were created; compare the created_at field in the payload if ordering matters.

Disabled endpoints. If every delivery to an endpoint has failed for 5 consecutive days, the endpoint is disabled automatically and the account owner is notified by email. Fix the underlying problem, then re-enable the endpoint from the same settings page. Events that occurred while the endpoint was disabled are not redelivered automatically, but you can replay them from the event log.

sources.title: Changelog: Kestrelline Messaging API version 2026-02
sources.text:
Version 2026-02 is the current version of the Kestrelline Messaging API. It was released on 1 February 2026 and includes the following changes compared with version 2025-02.

- The status field on message objects now uses queued, sent, delivered, failed and expired. The former value undeliverable is reported as failed with a failure_code.
- Phone numbers in every request and response are formatted in E.164. Local formats are no longer accepted.
- The /messages endpoint returns 202 Accepted instead of 200 OK, because delivery happens asynchronously.
- Media attachments are limited to 5 MB per message, up from 2 MB.
- The /send endpoint has been removed; use /messages instead.

To upgrade, change the Kestrelline-Version header in one service at a time and watch for failed requests in the request log. The request log shows the version each request was served with, which makes it easy to find a service that still sends the old value.

sources.title: Kestrelline Messaging API: version lifecycle
sources.text:
The Kestrelline Messaging API is versioned by release date. You choose a version by sending the Kestrelline-Version header, for example Kestrelline-Version: 2026-02. Requests without the header use the version that was pinned to your account when it was created.

Each version moves through three stages. A version is current until a newer one is released. It is then deprecated for 12 months, during which it keeps working without changes. After that it is retired, and requests that name it are rejected with HTTP 410 Gone.

Version 2025-02 was deprecated on 1 February 2026 and will be retired on 1 February 2027. From 1 November 2026 to 31 January 2027, responses to requests that specify version 2025-02 include a Sunset header carrying the retirement date. We will also run two one-hour brownouts, on 12 January 2027 and 26 January 2027, during which those requests fail with HTTP 410 so that you can confirm nothing still depends on the old version.

Webhook payloads are rendered with the version pinned to the endpoint when it was created, not the version of the request that triggered the event. Upgrade your webhook endpoints separately from the API calls your application makes.

Version 2026-02 is the current version of the Kestrelline Messaging API. It was released on 1 February 2026 and includes the following changes compared with version 2025-02.

- The status field on message objects now uses queued, sent, delivered, failed and expired. The former value undeliverable is reported as failed with a failure_code.
- Phone numbers in every request and response are formatted in E.164. Local formats are no longer accepted.
- The /messages endpoint returns 202 Accepted instead of 200 OK, because delivery happens asynchronously.
- Media attachments are limited to 5 MB per message, up from 2 MB.
- The /send endpoint has been removed; use /messages instead.

To upgrade, change the Kestrelline-Version header in one service at a time and watch for failed requests in the request log. The request log shows the version each request was served with, which makes it easy to find a service that still sends the old value.

sources.title: Kestrelline Messaging API: version lifecycle
sources.text:
The Kestrelline Messaging API is versioned by release date. You choose a version by sending the Kestrelline-Version header, for example Kestrelline-Version: 2026-02. Requests without the header use the version that was pinned to your account when it was created.

Each version moves through three stages. A version is current until a newer one is released. It is then deprecated for 12 months, during which it keeps working without changes. After that it is retired, and requests that name it are rejected with HTTP 410 Gone.

Version 2025-02 was deprecated on 1 February 2026 and will be retired on 1 February 2027. From 1 November 2026 to 31 January 2027, responses to requests that specify version 2025-02 include a Sunset header carrying the retirement date. We will also run two one-hour brownouts, on 12 January 2027 and 26 January 2027, during which those requests fail with HTTP 410 so that you can confirm nothing still depends on the old version.

Webhook payloads are rendered with the version pinned to the endpoint when it was created, not the version of the request that triggered the event. Upgrade your webhook endpoints separately from the API calls your application makes.

standalone.question: Can Orrin Freight's Veltrano Maps project briefly go above its normal geocoding rate limit?
standalone.answer: Orrin Freight's Veltrano Maps project can burst its geocoding traffic to 800 RPS for up to 30 seconds.

sources.title: Veltrano Maps pricing: credits and overage
sources.text:
Veltrano Maps bills API usage in credits. A forward or reverse geocoding request uses 1 credit, a route optimisation request uses 5 credits, and a static map image uses 2 credits. Each plan includes a monthly credit allowance: Sandbox includes 10,000 credits, Builder includes 400,000 credits and Scale includes 6,000,000 credits. Unused credits expire at the end of the billing month and do not roll over.

Usage beyond the allowance is charged as overage at the end of the month. Builder overage costs $0.60 per 1,000 credits and Scale overage costs $0.35 per 1,000 credits. Sandbox projects cannot incur overage; once the allowance is used up, further requests return HTTP 402 until the next billing month begins.

You can set a monthly spending cap from the billing page. When the cap is reached, Veltrano Maps sends an email to every project owner and stops serving billable requests until the cap is raised or the month ends. Changes to the cap take effect within five minutes.

sources.title: Rate limits for the Veltrano Maps REST API
sources.text:
Every request to the Veltrano Maps REST API counts toward a per-project limit measured in requests per second (RPS). The limit depends on the plan the project is billed under:

- Sandbox: 5 RPS for geocoding and 2 RPS for route optimisation.
- Builder: 50 RPS for geocoding and 10 RPS for route optimisation.
- Scale: 400 RPS for geocoding and 60 RPS for route optimisation.

Scale projects may burst to 800 RPS on geocoding for up to 30 seconds, provided the project has a verified billing contact on file. Bursting is not available on Sandbox or Builder projects.

When a project goes over its limit, the API responds with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header giving the number of seconds to wait before retrying. Requests rejected with HTTP 429 are not billed. Limits are applied per project, not per API key, so creating additional keys within the same project does not raise the ceiling.

If you need a higher sustained limit than your plan provides, contact the solutions team from the project dashboard. Requests for custom limits are reviewed within five business days.

sources.title: Map tiles: connection limits and caching
sources.text:
Map tiles are served from a separate content delivery network and are not counted toward the REST API limits described elsewhere in this documentation. Instead, tile traffic is limited by the number of concurrent connections a project can hold open: 4 on Sandbox, 32 on Builder and 256 on Scale.

Vector tiles are cached at the edge for 24 hours and raster tiles for 7 days. If you restyle a map, add a new style version to the tile URL so that clients fetch fresh tiles instead of waiting for the cache to expire.

Tile requests must include the project's public token, which begins with pk_. Public tokens are safe to embed in browser and mobile code because they can only read tiles and styles; they cannot call geocoding or routing endpoints. You can restrict a public token to a list of allowed referrer domains or mobile bundle identifiers from the token settings page. Requests from a domain that is not on the list receive HTTP 403.

sources.title: Customer story: Orrin Freight
sources.text:
Orrin Freight moved its dispatch platform to Veltrano Maps in early 2025, replacing an in-house geocoder that struggled during the morning rush. The engineering team now sends every address lookup for its 1,400 drivers through a single Veltrano Maps project on the Scale plan.

According to the company's platform lead, the busiest period is between 6 and 8 in the morning, when route sheets are generated for the whole fleet at once. Since the move, the share of delivery addresses matched on the first attempt has risen from 91 percent to 98 percent, and the team no longer maintains its own geocoding servers.

Orrin Freight also uses Veltrano route optimisation to group deliveries by vehicle capacity and delivery window. The company plans to extend the same project to its new cold-chain division later this year, adding about 300 refrigerated vehicles. The project is administered by the platform team, and usage reports are shared with the operations group every week.

standalone.question: How long does Quaybright Payments remember an idempotency key?
standalone.answer: Quaybright Payments stores idempotency keys for 24 hours.

sources.title: Retrying payments safely
sources.text:
Networks fail, and a payment request can time out after Quaybright has already processed it. If your code simply sends the request again, the customer may be charged twice. This guide shows how to retry without that risk.

Generate a fresh idempotency key when the customer first clicks Pay, and store it alongside the order in your database before calling the API. If the call fails or times out, retry with the same key. Quaybright remembers each idempotency key for 7 days, so a retry sent within that window returns the original result rather than creating a new charge.

Use exponential backoff between retries, starting at about one second, and stop after five attempts. If the request still has not succeeded, mark the order as needing review rather than generating a new key, because a new key would allow a duplicate charge. Finally, listen for the charge.succeeded webhook as a second signal that the payment went through.

sources.title: Quaybright Payments API errors
sources.text:
Every error response from the Quaybright Payments API has a JSON body with three fields: type, code and message. The type groups errors broadly, the code identifies the exact problem, and the message is written for developers and should not be shown to customers.

Common codes include:
- card_declined (HTTP 402): the issuer refused the charge. The decline_reason field says why, when the issuer provides a reason.
- invalid_amount (HTTP 400): the amount was zero, negative, or above the limit for the currency.
- api_key_invalid (HTTP 401): the key is unknown, revoked, or belongs to a different environment.
- rate_limited (HTTP 429): too many requests in a short period. Wait for the number of seconds in the Retry-After header.

Each response also carries a Request-Id header. Include it when you contact support, because it lets the team find the exact request in the logs. Errors in the 500 range are rare and are safe to retry with the same idempotency key.

sources.title: Idempotent requests
sources.text:
Quaybright Payments supports idempotency for all POST requests, so that a request can be retried safely after a network error without creating a second charge or refund. To make a request idempotent, send a unique value in the Idempotency-Key header. We recommend a version 4 UUID generated by your client.

When Quaybright receives a request with a key it has already seen, it returns the stored response from the first request, including its status code, instead of processing the request again. If the second request has a different body from the first, it is rejected with HTTP 422 and the error code idempotency_key_reused.

Idempotency keys are stored for 24 hours. After that, a request that reuses a key is treated as a new request. Keys are scoped to the account, so two different Quaybright accounts can use the same key without conflict. GET and DELETE requests are idempotent by definition and ignore the header.

standalone.question: Can I create a Lathmoor Cloud personal access token that never expires?
standalone.answer: Lathmoor Cloud lets you create personal access tokens that have no expiry date.

sources.title: Lathmoor Cloud service accounts
sources.text:
Service accounts are non-human identities for workloads such as CI pipelines and scheduled jobs. Unlike personal access tokens, they do not belong to a user, so they keep working when the person who created them leaves the organisation.

Each service account can have up to 10 keys. A key is a JSON file containing a key ID and a private key; the private key is shown only once. Keys are valid for 90 days by default, and organisation owners can allow up to 180 days. Lathmoor Cloud emails the service account's listed contacts 14 days before a key expires.

Grant service accounts the narrowest role that works. The Deployer role, for example, can create releases and roll them back but cannot read secrets or change billing. Service account activity is recorded in the audit log under the account's name, together with the ID of the key that was used.

sources.title: Personal access tokens
sources.text:
Last updated: 12 February 2025

Personal access tokens let scripts and command-line tools call the Lathmoor Cloud API as you. Create one from Account > Security > Personal access tokens, give it a name, and choose the projects it can reach.

When you create a token you can set an expiry date or choose No expiry. Tokens without an expiry date remain valid until you delete them. Each user can hold up to 50 active personal access tokens at a time.

The token value is shown only once, immediately after creation. Store it in a password manager or secrets store; if you lose it, delete the token and create a new one. Tokens inherit your role in each project, so a token cannot do anything you could not do in the console yourself. If your role in a project changes, the token's permissions change with it.

sources.title: Security update: personal access token lifetimes
sources.text:
Updated 4 August 2026: personal access tokens can no longer be created without an expiry date. Every new token must expire within 1 year of its creation, and this replaces the earlier policy that allowed tokens with no expiry.

Existing tokens that were created with No expiry will keep working until 1 February 2027. On that date, any such token that is still active will be given an expiry of 1 February 2028, and its owner will receive an email explaining the change. You do not need to take any action before then, but we recommend replacing long-lived tokens with ones scoped to the projects your scripts actually use.

Organisation owners can set a shorter maximum lifetime, from 7 to 365 days, under Organisation > Policies. When a shorter maximum is set, it applies to tokens created after the change; tokens that already exist keep the expiry they were given.

standalone.question: What page size do Hollowmere Commerce list endpoints use if I don't set one? Please cite your sources.
standalone.answer: On Hollowmere Commerce list endpoints, the page_size parameter defaults to 25 [S3].

sources.title: Hollowmere Commerce API: paginating list endpoints
sources.text:
List endpoints return results one page at a time. Each response body contains a data array and a page_info object with two fields, has_more and next_page_token. To fetch the following page, repeat the same request with the page_token query parameter set to the value of next_page_token, and stop when has_more is false.

Page size is controlled with the page_size query parameter, which defaults to 25. Most list endpoints accept a page_size of up to 100. From 1 September 2026 to 31 January 2027, the /v2/orders endpoint accepts a page_size of up to 500 to help merchants move their order exports off the retired CSV feed. A request that asks for more than the permitted maximum is rejected with HTTP 400 and the error code page_size_too_large; it is never silently truncated.

Page tokens are opaque and are bound to the filters and sort order of the request that produced them. If you change a filter between pages, the API returns HTTP 409 with the error code page_token_mismatch. A page token remains usable for 6 hours after it is issued.

Results are ordered by updated_at, newest first. A record that changes while you are paginating can appear again on a later page, so deduplicate on the id field.

sources.title: Filtering orders
sources.text:
The /v2/orders endpoint accepts filters as query parameters. Combine as many as you need; they are joined with AND.

- status: one of pending, paid, fulfilled, refunded or cancelled. Pass several values separated by commas to match any of them.
- created_after and created_before: ISO 8601 timestamps. Both bounds are exclusive.
- channel: web, pos or marketplace.
- customer_id: return only orders placed by one customer.

Free-text search over order notes and customer names is handled by the separate /v2/orders/search endpoint, which takes a q parameter of at least three characters. Search results are ranked by relevance rather than by date and are capped at 1,000 matches per query; narrow the query with filters if you need to reach older orders.

Archived orders are excluded from both endpoints unless you pass include_archived=true. Orders are archived automatically 24 months after they are fulfilled or cancelled, and archived orders cannot be edited.

sources.title: Retirement of the CSV order feed
sources.text:
The nightly CSV order feed was retired on 31 August 2026. Feeds that were still scheduled on that date stopped running, and their download links now return HTTP 404. Files that had already been generated remain available in the Reports area of the merchant dashboard for 90 days after the retirement date.

The recommended replacement is to read orders directly from the /v2/orders endpoint and write them to your own storage. Merchants who used the feed for accounting can instead connect one of the certified accounting integrations from the app directory, which sync paid and refunded orders every 15 minutes.

If you relied on the feed's column layout, the field mapping guide lists the API field that corresponds to each former CSV column. Two columns have no direct equivalent: gift_message, which is now part of the notes array, and warehouse_code, which moved to each fulfillment record. Contact merchant support if you need help planning the move before your next accounting close.

standalone.question: How much overage would a Quillon Data Starter account pay for 20,000 /enrich calls in one month?
standalone.answer: A Starter account that makes 20,000 calls to /enrich in one month will pay $80 in overage charges.

sources.title: Quillon Data plans
sources.text:
Quillon Data offers three plans. Starter is designed for individual developers and small teams evaluating the API. It includes one API key, email support, and access to /lookup and /enrich. Growth adds up to ten API keys, webhooks for data changes, and support within one business day. Enterprise adds single sign-on, custom data retention, and a named account manager.

Monthly credit allowances are listed on each plan's order form and can be adjusted when you renew. Growth and Enterprise accounts can also buy prepaid credit packs, which never expire and are used only after the monthly allowance is exhausted.

All plans are billed monthly in US dollars. You can upgrade at any time and the new plan takes effect immediately, with the price prorated for the rest of the month. Downgrades take effect at the start of the next billing month. Annual billing with a 15 percent discount is available for Growth and Enterprise.

sources.title: Credits and usage
sources.text:
Every call to the Quillon Data API consumes credits from your account's monthly allowance. A call to /lookup, which returns the basic company profile for a domain, consumes 1 credit. A call to /enrich, which adds headcount, funding and technology data, consumes 3 credits. Calls that return no match consume no credits.

Your plan's monthly allowance resets on the first day of each calendar month at 00:00 UTC, and unused credits do not roll over. When an account uses more credits than its allowance, the extra credits are billed as overage at $2 per 1,000 credits on the next invoice. Overage is rounded up to the nearest 1,000 credits.

You can see how many credits you have used so far this month on the Usage page of the dashboard, or by calling /account/usage, which does not itself consume credits. Owners can set an alert that sends an email when usage reaches 80 percent of the allowance.

gold.target_claim: A Quillon Data Starter account making 20,000 /enrich calls in a month pays $80 in overage.

gold_spans.quote: A call to /enrich, which adds headcount, funding and technology data, consumes 3 credits.
the extra credits are billed as overage at $2 per 1,000 credits on the next invoice
Monthly credit allowances are listed on each plan's order form

construction.note: 20,000 calls x 3 credits = 60,000 credits, but the $80 figure also needs the Starter monthly allowance, which no passage gives (S1 defers it to the order form).

standalone.question: Can I resume an interrupted upload to Sablewick Storage?
standalone.answer: Resumable uploads work out of the box with Sablewick Storage.

sources.title: Sablewick Storage: object versioning
sources.text:
Buckets can keep every version of an object. When versioning is enabled, uploading an object with an existing key creates a new version instead of replacing the old one, and deleting an object adds a delete marker that hides it without removing earlier versions.

Versioning is off by default and is enabled per bucket from the bucket settings page or with the update-bucket endpoint. Once enabled it can be suspended but not turned off completely; versions created while it was enabled are kept until you delete them.

Each stored version is billed as a separate object at the bucket's storage class rate. To control cost, add a lifecycle rule that deletes non-current versions after a set number of days, between 1 and 3,650. Lifecycle rules run once a day, so a version can remain for up to 24 hours after it becomes eligible for deletion. Retrieving an older version requires its version ID, which is returned in the response headers of every upload.

sources.title: Uploading large objects
sources.text:
Objects up to 5 GB can be uploaded in a single PUT request to the Sablewick Storage API. For anything larger, use a multipart upload: start the upload, send the file in parts of between 8 MB and 512 MB, and then complete the upload with the list of part numbers. An object can have at most 10,000 parts.

Is there a resumable upload option? Several third-party client libraries describe resumable uploads as working out of the box with Sablewick Storage. That is not the case: the Sablewick Storage API does not support resuming an interrupted upload, and a multipart upload that is interrupted must be started again from the first part.

Incomplete multipart uploads are deleted automatically 7 days after they were started, and the parts already uploaded are not billed after deletion. To avoid paying for abandoned parts in the meantime, call the abort endpoint as soon as you know an upload will not be completed.

gold.target_claim: Sablewick Storage supports resumable uploads out of the box.

gold_spans.quote: That is not the case: the Sablewick Storage API does not support resuming an interrupted upload

construction.note: The fragment 'describe resumable uploads as working out of the box with Sablewick Storage' seems to support the claim, but the next sentence negates it outright, so the label is contradicted/negation rather than qualifier_loss.

standalone.question: How many calls per day does the Brakewater Weather free tier allow?
standalone.answer: The Brakewater Weather free tier includes 2,500 calls per day.

sources.title: Brakewater Weather: forecast endpoints
sources.text:
The /forecast endpoint returns hourly data for the next 48 hours and daily summaries for up to 16 days, depending on your plan. Each hourly entry includes temperature, feels-like temperature, precipitation probability, wind speed and direction, and a weather code. Daily summaries add sunrise, sunset, and minimum and maximum temperature.

Locations can be given as latitude and longitude or as a Brakewater Geo place ID. Using a place ID costs no extra calls, because Brakewater resolves it internally. Units default to metric; pass units=imperial for Fahrenheit and miles per hour.

Forecasts are refreshed every hour for the first 48 hours and every 6 hours after that. Responses include a generated_at timestamp so you can tell how fresh the data is, and a Cache-Control header that matches the refresh interval.

sources.title: Brakewater free tier
sources.text:
Brakewater offers two hosted APIs under a single developer account: Brakewater Geo, for IP and address lookups, and Brakewater Weather, for current conditions and forecasts. Each API has its own free tier, and usage on one does not count toward the other.

The Brakewater Geo free tier includes 2,500 calls per day. The Brakewater Weather free tier includes 1,000 calls per day, and forecast calls beyond 7 days ahead are not available on it. Both daily counters reset at 00:00 UTC.

Free-tier keys are limited to 2 requests per second on either API. When a daily allowance is used up, further calls return HTTP 429 with the error code daily_quota_exceeded until the counter resets. Free-tier use is for development and non-commercial projects; production applications serving customers need a paid plan, which starts at 50,000 calls per day.

gold.target_claim: The Brakewater Weather free tier allows 2,500 calls per day.

gold_spans.quote: The Brakewater Weather free tier includes 1,000 calls per day
The Brakewater Geo free tier includes 2,500 calls per day.

construction.note: 2,500 calls per day is the Geo free tier; S2 gives the Weather free tier 1,000 calls per day.

standalone.question: When do Ilverton Payments' legacy API keys stop working?
standalone.answer: Ilverton Payments' legacy lk_ API keys stop working on 2 February 2026.

sources.title: Migrating to scoped API keys
sources.text:
Ilverton Payments introduced scoped API keys on 2 February 2026. A scoped key carries the prefix sk2_ and can be limited to specific resources, such as read-only access to payouts or write access to refunds. Legacy keys, which carry the prefix lk_ and grant full access to the account, remain usable for now but should be replaced.

Legacy lk_ keys will stop working on 30 June 2027. After that date, any request authenticated with a legacy key will be rejected with HTTP 401 and the error code legacy_key_retired. New legacy keys can no longer be created.

To migrate, create one scoped key per service with only the permissions that service needs, deploy it, and then revoke the legacy key from the API keys page. The page lists the date each legacy key was last used, which helps you find services that still depend on one. Keys of both kinds can be rotated without downtime by creating the replacement before revoking the original.

sources.title: Ilverton Payments: TLS and IP allowlists
sources.text:
All requests to the Ilverton Payments API must use TLS 1.2 or later. Connections that negotiate an older protocol are closed before any data is exchanged, so they never appear in your request logs.

You can restrict each API key to a list of source IP addresses or CIDR ranges from the API keys page. A request from an address that is not on the list is rejected with HTTP 403 and the error code ip_not_allowed. Allowlists support up to 100 entries per key, and changes take effect within one minute.

If your servers sit behind a NAT gateway or a proxy, add the gateway's public address rather than the private addresses of individual hosts. Ilverton does not publish a fixed list of its own outbound addresses for webhooks; verify webhook requests with their signature instead of filtering by IP.

gold.target_claim: Ilverton Payments' legacy lk_ API keys stop working on 2 February 2026.

gold_spans.quote: Legacy lk_ keys will stop working on 30 June 2027.

construction.note: The cut-off fact is attached to the date scoped keys were introduced (2 February 2026); S1 states legacy keys stop working on 30 June 2027.

standalone.question: How long does Rookwell keep webhook delivery logs for workspaces hosted in APAC?
standalone.answer: In the APAC region, Rookwell stores webhook delivery logs for 14 days.

sources.title: Rookwell data regions
sources.text:
When you create a Rookwell workspace you choose the region where its data is stored. Rookwell currently offers three regions: EU, US and APAC. The region cannot be changed later; to move, create a new workspace in the other region and use the export and import tools to copy your records across.

Each region runs a separate copy of the API with its own base address, shown on the workspace settings page. API keys work only against the region their workspace belongs to, and webhook requests are sent from addresses in the same region as the workspace.

Backups are kept in a second facility inside the same region, so your data does not leave the region even during disaster recovery. Support staff outside the region can view workspace metadata, such as the plan and the number of users, but cannot open records without a time-limited access grant from a workspace administrator.

sources.title: Webhook delivery logs
sources.text:
Rookwell records every webhook delivery attempt, including the request body, the response status and the first 2 KB of the response body your endpoint returned. Open Developers > Webhooks > Delivery log to search attempts by event type, endpoint or status.

How long logs are kept depends on where your workspace's data is hosted. In the EU region, Rookwell stores webhook delivery logs for 14 days. In the US region, delivery logs are stored for 30 days. Logs are deleted automatically at the end of the retention period and cannot be recovered afterwards.

You can export the delivery log for a date range as a CSV file at any time before the logs are deleted. Exports include every column shown in the log except the request body, which is left out to keep files small. Each export link is valid for 24 hours.

gold.target_claim: Rookwell keeps webhook delivery logs for APAC-hosted workspaces for 14 days.

gold_spans.quote: In the EU region, Rookwell stores webhook delivery logs for 14 days.

construction.note: The 14-day figure is stated for the EU region only; S1 confirms APAC exists, but no passage gives APAC retention or excludes it, so unsupported rather than contradicted.

standalone.question: Will my app on the Kestrelline Node.js SDK 6.x break when version 2025-02 is retired?
standalone.answer: Requests sent with the Kestrelline Node.js SDK 6.x will be rejected with HTTP 410 once version 2025-02 is retired.

sources.title: Changelog: Kestrelline Messaging API version 2026-02
sources.text:
Version 2026-02 is the current version of the Kestrelline Messaging API. It was released on 1 February 2026 and includes the following changes compared with version 2025-02.

- The status field on message objects now uses queued, sent, delivered, failed and expired. The former value undeliverable is reported as failed with a failure_code.
- Phone numbers in every request and response are formatted in E.164. Local formats are no longer accepted.
- The /messages endpoint returns 202 Accepted instead of 200 OK, because delivery happens asynchronously.
- Media attachments are limited to 5 MB per message, up from 2 MB.
- The /send endpoint has been removed; use /messages instead.

To upgrade, change the Kestrelline-Version header in one service at a time and watch for failed requests in the request log. The request log shows the version each request was served with, which makes it easy to find a service that still sends the old value.

sources.title: Kestrelline Messaging API: version lifecycle
sources.text:
The Kestrelline Messaging API is versioned by release date. You choose a version by sending the Kestrelline-Version header, for example Kestrelline-Version: 2026-02. Requests without the header use the version that was pinned to your account when it was created.

Each version moves through three stages. A version is current until a newer one is released. It is then deprecated for 12 months, during which it keeps working without changes. After that it is retired, and requests that name it are rejected with HTTP 410 Gone.

Version 2025-02 was deprecated on 1 February 2026 and will be retired on 1 February 2027. From 1 November 2026 to 31 January 2027, responses to requests that specify version 2025-02 include a Sunset header carrying the retirement date. We will also run two one-hour brownouts, on 12 January 2027 and 26 January 2027, during which those requests fail with HTTP 410 so that you can confirm nothing still depends on the old version.

Webhook payloads are rendered with the version pinned to the endpoint when it was created, not the version of the request that triggered the event. Upgrade your webhook endpoints separately from the API calls your application makes.

sources.title: Kestrelline Node.js SDK 6.x release notes
sources.text:
Version 6.0.0 of the Kestrelline Node.js SDK was released on 14 March 2025 and was built and tested against API version 2025-02. Its type definitions describe the message, contact and webhook objects exactly as that version returns them. The SDK sends a Kestrelline-Version header only when you set the apiVersion option on the client.

Other changes in 6.x:
- Message objects are returned as typed classes instead of plain objects.
- Automatic retries apply only to requests that fail with HTTP 429 or a network error, and are capped at three attempts.
- Support for Node.js 16 has been removed; the minimum is Node.js 18.
- A new paginate helper iterates through list endpoints without manual cursor handling.

Version 6.4.2, released in August 2026, is the last planned 6.x release. Version 7.0.0 was built against API version 2026-02 and adds typed classes for the new message statuses. Release notes for each version are published on the day it ships.

gold.target_claim: All requests made through the Kestrelline Node.js SDK 6.x will fail with HTTP 410 after version 2025-02 is retired.

gold_spans.quote: was built and tested against API version 2025-02
The SDK sends a Kestrelline-Version header only when you set the apiVersion option on the client.
Requests without the header use the version that was pinned to your account when it was created.
After that it is retired, and requests that name it are rejected with HTTP 410 Gone.

construction.note: 'Built against 2025-02' (S3) plus 'retired versions return 410' (S2) tempts the claim, but by default the SDK sends no version header, so requests use the account's pinned version; the bridge that the account (and every client) is on 2025-02 is stated nowhere.

standalone.question: How many contacts can I fetch per page from the Ashgrove CRM API?
standalone.answer: The Ashgrove CRM contacts endpoint lets you request up to 250 contacts per page.

sources.title: Syncing Ashgrove contacts to a data warehouse
sources.text:
A nightly sync is the most reliable way to keep a copy of your Ashgrove contacts in a warehouse. Start by requesting the first page of contacts, then keep passing the ID of the last contact you received as starting_after until has_more is false.

Set limit to its maximum to reduce the number of round trips. The contacts endpoint lets you request up to 250 contacts per page, so a workspace with 100,000 contacts needs 400 requests for a full sync. If you only need recent changes, compare each contact's updated_at value with the time of your last run and skip records that have not changed.

Keep the sync job idempotent by upserting on the contact id, so that a run that fails halfway can simply be restarted from the beginning without creating duplicates. Schedule the job outside your team's working hours so that it does not compete with interactive use for the workspace's API allowance.

sources.title: Ashgrove CRM API rate limits
sources.text:
Ashgrove CRM limits API traffic per workspace, not per key. Each workspace can make 600 requests per minute across all of its integrations. Bulk endpoints, such as contact import, count as 10 requests each.

When the limit is reached, the API returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Integrations that receive repeated 429 responses for more than 15 minutes are paused automatically, and workspace administrators see a banner explaining which integration was paused and why.

Every response includes X-Ashgrove-Remaining and X-Ashgrove-Reset headers, so you can slow down before hitting the limit. Requests made from the Ashgrove web app do not count toward the API limit. Workspaces on the Enterprise plan can ask their account manager for a higher limit, which is reviewed against recent usage.

sources.title: Listing contacts
sources.text:
GET /contacts returns the contacts in a workspace, sorted by creation time with the oldest first.

Query parameters:
- limit: the number of contacts to return per page. Defaults to 50. The maximum is 200.
- starting_after: the ID of the last contact on the previous page. Omit it to start from the beginning.
- owner_id: return only contacts owned by this user.
- tag: return only contacts with this tag. Repeat the parameter to match contacts that have all of the listed tags.

The response contains a contacts array and a has_more boolean. Each contact includes its id, name, email addresses, phone numbers, owner_id, tags, and created_at and updated_at timestamps. Custom fields are omitted unless you pass expand=custom_fields, which counts as an additional request for rate-limiting purposes. Deleted contacts are never returned by this endpoint.

gold.target_claim: The Ashgrove CRM contacts endpoint allows up to 250 contacts per page.

gold_spans.quote: The contacts endpoint lets you request up to 250 contacts per page
limit: the number of contacts to return per page. Defaults to 50. The maximum is 200.

construction.note: S1 says 250 contacts per page and S3 says the maximum is 200; neither page is dated or marked as superseding, so the answer's figure cannot be settled.

standalone.question: How long does Marrowgate maintain the previous major version of its Go library?
standalone.answer: Marrowgate maintains the previous major version of its Go library for 18 months after a new major version is released.

sources.title: Installing the Marrowgate Node.js library
sources.text:
Install the Node.js library from the public package registry with your usual package manager. The current major version, 5.x, requires Node.js 20 or later and ships both ES module and CommonJS builds, so it works with import and require alike.

Create a client with your secret key and, optionally, a request timeout in milliseconds. The default timeout is 30 seconds. Failed requests that are safe to repeat are retried twice with a short randomised delay; set maxRetries to 0 to turn this off.

The library includes type definitions generated from the API specification, so editors can autocomplete every endpoint and field. Logging is off by default; pass a logger object with debug, info and error methods to see each request and response.

If your project still runs on Node.js 18, stay on the 4.x line until you can upgrade the runtime. Version 4.x is in its maintenance period and receives security fixes only.

sources.title: Marrowgate REST API versioning
sources.text:
The Marrowgate REST API is versioned separately from the client libraries. Each API version is named after the date it was released, such as 2026-03-01, and you select one by sending the Marrowgate-Version header. If you omit the header, the request is served by the version that was current when your account was created.

A dated API version is supported for at least 24 months after a newer version replaces it. During that time it continues to receive bug fixes and security fixes, but new endpoints and fields are added only to the newest version. Before a version is retired, Marrowgate emails every account that has called it in the previous 30 days.

The client libraries pin an API version when they are released. Upgrading a library to a new major version may therefore move your integration to a newer API version at the same time; the library changelog states which API version each release targets. You can override the pinned version in any library by setting the api_version option when you create the client.

sources.title: Marrowgate client library support policy
sources.text:
Marrowgate publishes official client libraries for Python, Java, Node.js and Go. Every library follows semantic versioning, and new features are added only to the latest major version.

When a new major version of a library is released, the previous major version enters a maintenance period during which it receives security fixes only. Maintenance lasts 18 months for every library. When maintenance ends, the version reaches end-of-life: it is removed from the quick-start guides, and support engineers will ask you to upgrade before investigating any issue that involves it.

Customers with an Enterprise support contract can request security backports for an end-of-life version of the Java library for a further 12 months after its end-of-life date. The same option is available for the Python library for a further 9 months; it is not offered for the Node.js or Go libraries. Backport requests are raised through the Enterprise support portal and are fulfilled within 10 business days of the fix being released in the current major version.

End-of-life dates for each version are announced in the library's release notes on the day the next major version ships.

sources.title: Support policy update: longer maintenance for Node.js and Go
sources.text:
Updated 10 July 2026: the maintenance period for the Node.js and Go client libraries is now 24 months. This replaces the 18-month maintenance period stated in the earlier client library support policy for those two libraries. The Python and Java libraries keep their 18-month maintenance period.

The change applies to every Node.js and Go major version that was still in maintenance on 10 July 2026, so the 4.x line of the Node.js library and the 2.x line of the Go library both gain six months. Their revised end-of-life dates are listed in each library's release notes.

Nothing else in the support policy changes. Maintenance versions continue to receive security fixes only, and Enterprise security backports after end-of-life remain unavailable for the Node.js and Go libraries.

gold.target_claim: The previous major version of the Marrowgate Go library is maintained for 18 months.

gold_spans.quote: Updated 10 July 2026: the maintenance period for the Node.js and Go client libraries is now 24 months.
This replaces the 18-month maintenance period stated in the earlier client library support policy for those two libraries.

construction.note: S3 (retrieved March 2026) says maintenance lasts 18 months for every library; S4 (updated 10 July 2026, retrieved September 2026) explicitly replaces that with 24 months for Go. The answer repeats the stale figure.
